_comment: WHAT A GNAWED GAP OPENS INTO. A cellar with the walls closer in: fewer rooms, tighter, the rooms closer together so a run between them is a squeeze rather than a walk. Browner and warmer than poured concrete, because this is bedding rather than building. Spacing is in TILES, so the cellar's distances inherited into a smaller box leave nowhere to seat the second hole a floor is guaranteed -- a tighter space needs them tighter. Its holes lean gnawed, which is what makes a warren feel like a NETWORK -- more of it runs sideways than down -- and rooms_per_floor is how many rooms a warren spreads to on one floor before the space stops offering ways sideways. tile_visuals 0 is the floor and 1 is the wall, and that is the whole set: a wall is a flat block, and which way a hole goes is said by the HOLE, drawn at the angle it is seen from. A type may name a `tileset` (an LDtk tileset identifier) whose cells are found by their enum tags; an id with no tagged cell falls back to the colour here.
